introduction.p: Suppose that you are driving a car on the highway using cruise control so that you drive at a constant speed. The time, T (measured in hours), it takes to drive 50 miles depends on the constant rate, s (measured in miles per hour) at which you are driving. Since

static.solution:
T_2(x) is the second degree Taylor polynomial for f(x) about x=0, T_2(0)=f(0), which says c_0=f(0). Since \frac{d}{dx}T_2(x) \big|_{x=0} = f'(0), c_1=f'(0); and since \frac{d^2}{dx^2} T_2(x) \big|_{x=0} = f''(0), 2c_2=f''(0). In other words, c_0 is the y-intercept of f(x), c_1 is the slope of the tangent line to f(x) at x=0 and c_2 tells us the concavity of f(x) near x=0.
Thus c_0 > 0; c_1 \lt 0; and c_2 > 0

over

Using the Lagrange Error Bound for T_n(x), calculate:

solution.p: The n^{th} degree approximation of f(1.02) about x=1 is given by:
f''(x) is always positive in the interval [1,1.02] so T_{2}(1.02) is a overestimate of f(1.02).
Using the Lagrange Error Bound we find an M such that:
\left|f(1.02)-T_{2}(1.02)\right| \le \frac{M}{3 !}\left|1.02-1\right|^{3}, where M \ge \left|f^{3}(t)\right| for all t in the interval [1,1.02].
By examining \left|f'''(x)\right| we find that it is biggest when t=1. Therefore, a suitable choice is M=f'''(1).

statement.p: Calculate the integral:

static.solution: \frac{1}{(x+2)(x+6)}=\frac{A}{x+2}+\frac{B}{x+6}, giving 1 = A(x+6)+B(x+2), or 1 = (A+B)x+ (6 A+2 B). Solving for A and B, we find A = 0.25 and B = -0.25, so \int \frac{1}{(x+2)(x+6)}\,dx= \int\frac{0.25}{x+2}\,dx + \int \frac{-0.25}{x+6}\,dx = 0.25\ln\mathopen{}\left(\left|x+2\right|\right)-0.25\ln\mathopen{}\left(\left|x+6\right|\right)+C.
